display.purpose: The one question at the top of Discover ("What's for dinner?"), with the meal word in Bold.

title.purpose: Section headings, including step sections in Directions and cook mode.

row-title.purpose: Recipe names in lists and cards.

cook-step.purpose: Step text in cook mode, read from arm's length.

label.purpose: Buttons, pills, counts and tab labels.

hand.purpose: Greetings, signposts, encouragement, empty states. Never facts.

shadows.name: lift
shadows.purpose: Photos, round action buttons, the heart and the pinned bar only.

shadows.name: lift-dark
shadows.purpose: The same lift in dark mode.

motion.name: spring
motion.purpose: Press feedback with a small overshoot: card straighten, heart pop, tab icon hop.

motion.name: glide
motion.purpose: Settling motion with no overshoot: the time-picker highlight, layout.

motion.name: trail-draw
motion.purpose: The dotted trail draws in from the left after a card lands.

motion.name: reduce-motion
motion.purpose: Under Reduce Motion every motion is replaced by its still end state, not a faster version.

breakpoints.name: larger-text
breakpoints.purpose: Trail card titles take a third line.

narrative.overview:
Cooking here is a walk, not a test. Recipes sit along a trail, quickest first, with handwritten signposts for time. Cuisines become journeys you hike from easy to summit, with refugios where you rest and learn a technique. The ground is warm sand paper; the planting is garden green; the drawings are ink lines by hand. A small tuxedo cat keeps you company on the trail, in cook mode and on journeys, and nowhere else.

The app is a calm kitchen tool, not a feed. Density is low and deliberate: one question per screen ("What's for dinner?"), one big action per screen ("Start cooking"), and everything else quiet. Personality lives in the details the cook meets while waiting or after finishing (signposts, the cat, the stirring pot, a pencil line through a ticked ingredient), never in the way of an instruction. In cook mode the phone is propped up and hands are messy, so the app switches to a dark charcoal page with very large step text, amounts inline, and voice.
keyCharacteristics: Sand paper ground with garden greens; no blues next to food.
Serif for names and headings, Rubik for anything you act on, handwriting only for warmth.
Ink-line drawings (ingredients, equipment, doodles) in one stroke weight.
Photos float on a soft shadow; the interface itself is flat.
Soft, rounded, pressable controls with a small spring and a light haptic.
One helper cat, only in cook mode and on journeys.

rules.name: The Food Comes First Rule
rules.body: No blues and no saturated accents anywhere near food photos. Greens and sand only, so the food is the brightest thing on screen.

rules.name: The Ink On Fill Rule
rules.body: Small text is always dark ink. Sage and green are for filled shapes; the only colored text is Deep Moss.

rules.name: The Feelings, Not Facts Rule
rules.body: Handwriting is for warmth: greetings, signposts, encouragement, empty states. Anything the cook needs to act on or read precisely (counts, amounts, voice hints, errors, instructions) is in Rubik.

rules.name: The Android Clip Rule
rules.body: Handwritten text on Android always gets `textBreakStrategy="simple"`, a few pixels of right padding, and a line limit, or its last glyph clips.

rules.name: The Whole Words Rule
rules.body: Text follows Dynamic Type and Android font scale, and nothing that carries meaning truncates at 2.0×. Content text (titles, steps, ingredient lines) always scales fully and gains a line rather than an ellipsis: trail card titles take 3 lines above 1.3×, hike titles 3. Only chrome that shares a fixed row may cap its growth, and it still grows: tab labels to 1.4×, time-picker labels to 1.5×, signpost boards to 1.2×. Test large text only after relaunching the app; a font-scale change while the app is running leaves stale measurements that look like clipping.

rules.name: The Photos Float Rule
rules.body: Only photos and the few floating controls get a shadow. Cards, chips, sheets and panels are flat and tinted.

dos: Do keep one primary action per screen, in Sage Leaf with ink text.
Do put amounts, times and temperatures in tags so they're found by shape; keep small text in ink.
Do use the category tint for recipe cards and rows, and Dry Sand for informational panels.
Do give every motion a Reduce Motion fallback (still, not just faster).
Do keep the cook's messy hands in mind: big targets, inline amounts, voice, nothing that needs precise taps.
Do make on/off chips say what "on" means: a tick on Sage Leaf for things you have, a cross in an ink outline for things to avoid, with a plain summary line ("Avoiding: soy").

Do round scaled amounts the way each measure works: cups in quarters and thirds, tablespoons in halves, teaspoons down to ⅛; cloves and eggs whole, cans and blocks in halves, produce in quarters. Never scale below what can be measured.
Do write the grocery list in shopping words ("jasmine rice", "1 lime"), with cooking notes ("for 1 cup cooked", "optional") as a quiet second line.
Do give anything that removes or counts something a way back: Undo, Reset, "Take one off", "Come back to it".

Do style text actions by what they do: underlined green text only navigates ("See all", guide links); actions that change your data (Mark it cooked, Take one off, Undo, Reset, Take another path) are small outline chips.
Do teach at the point of use with one-time hints: a Dry Sand note with a ✕, dismissed for good when closed or when the cook uses the feature. Never a tour, never twice.
Do treat a summit as a memory: once reached it stays (postcard, date), and the trail shows any stops reopened beside it.
donts: Don't use blue or saturated accents near food.
Don't set counts, amounts, instructions, voice hints or errors in the handwriting font.
Don't put shadows on cards, chips or panels; only photos and floating controls lift.
Don't show the live cat outside cook mode and journey pages, or let it cover text. On keepsakes (the trail postcard) it is a still drawing.

Don't add streaks, badges, rewards, confetti or nudges; cooked counts stay quiet records. The Kitchen's record is one plain Graphite sentence ("You've cooked 10 meals from 4 recipes and summited 1 hike."), never a row of big numbers, and it's absent before the first cook.
Don't use pills for status; status is a tag, a stamp or plain text.
